answer: A new identity spends its first 3 epochs on probation, during which its attestations count for 35% of full weight. Because the ripple weight is recomputed from the harbor history each close, the quill audit shows the reduced figure and the promotion is earned rather than bought. Running a farm hence buys partial influence at full price for each alias, and the discount only arrives after the operator has already paid the bond. That is 2 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
